articles.title: Alice Zaslavsky’s satay-butter charred cabbage wedges with fragrant chicken mince – recipe
articles.summary: The cookbook author has a shortcut method for blanching vegetables that saves on time, equipment and water. Check out more Alice Zaslavsky recipes. I love a burnt brassica, and there’s no better flavour than the big mama herself: the cabbage.
body: Vegetables in the cruciferous family, like brussels sprouts, broccoli and cauliflower, have naturally bitter compounds. However, with concentrated heat, this bitterness is transformed into sweetly caramelised corners and burnished bits.
It’s one way to make brassica boo-ers braver. But getting cooked-through cabbage with a softened heart and gnarly edges requires a delicate balance of time under heat.

Lucky for us, the sharp bitterness of cabbage has been bred out of more conventional styles on supermarket and greengrocer shelves. Modern varieties are much milder, sweeter and less fibrous, meaning they require far less cooking than the cabbages of old.
That’s why these days, I’m fond of a gentler method that softens their rawness without overcooking: the kettle-blanch.

articles.title: ‘As creamy as Haagen Dazs’: I tried three affordable ice-cream machines – the $24 beat them all
articles.summary: From the portable My Mug to the sleek Soft Serve Machine, I reviewed the Dash ice-cream makers worth your freezer space. Sign up for the Filter US newsletter, your weekly guide to buying fewer, better things. Soft serve always feels like a special occasion.
body: Naturally I’m thrilled to see soft serve has enjoyed a renaissance, especially in my city. Last year, cronut creator Dominique Ansel made waves with soft serve dipped in French butter. Soft serve margaritas took over TikTok this year. And if line culture is any indication of interest, soft serve spots like Culture and, in my neighborhood, Lisbonata, now draw round-the-block throngs of treat seekers.

Rather than spending hours (and a small fortune) waiting in line, I decided to see if I could spin up some decent soft serve in my own kitchen. But these machines, such as Ninja’s buzzy Creami Scoop and Swirl, can be pricey, and I couldn’t stomach the $349 cost for something we’d probably only end up using a few times a year (though the cult of Creami may argue it’s worth it ).

Enter Dash, a budget appliance brand known for its $11 mini waffle makers. I decided to try its line of ultra-affordable frozen dessert machines: the Soft Serve Ice Cream Maker, Deluxe Gelato & Ice Cream Maker and compact My Mug.

articles.title: Curbs on vertical drinking in Soho pubs to go ahead as Khan criticises council’s ‘breathtaking arrogance’
articles.summary: Exclusive: London mayor accuses council of ‘ignoring’ responses to a consultation. Sadiq Khan has criticised the “breathtaking arrogance” of Westminster council, which has kept restrictions on vertical drinking in Soho and an effective ban on new bars and pubs in the area.
body: The mayor of London has accused the Conservative-led council of “ignoring” the responses to a consultation into its new licensing policy. The vast majority of respondents, 81%, disagreed with the council’s “cumulative impact zone” which decrees that applications for bars and pubs in the West End of London, one of Europe’s most famous nightlife districts, will be refused unless in exceptional circumstances. Eighty-four per cent said the licensing policy would be bad for business.

Respondents also criticised the council’s position on “vertical drinking”, which is standing up to have a beverage, a common practice in British pubs. The council proposed, to widespread outcry, that new licences for pubs and bars should be granted to those venues which have table service instead of ordering at the bar, and those in which people are seated rather than standing.

The mayor had responded to a consultation held this summer by the council and ordered them to scrap the cumulative impact zone and allow pubs and bars to have space for vertical drinking. Andy Burnham, the prime minister, also waded into the row, saying vertical drinking is “British life”.
points: Sadiq Khan has criticised the “breathtaking arrogance” of Westminster council, which has kept restrictions on vertical drinking in Soho and an effective ban on new bars and pubs in the area.

articles.title: Want to borrow a dinosaur fossil? Try California’s one-of-a-kind taxidermy lending library
articles.summary: A natural history museum lets residents take home 1,400 specimens, from bobcats and beetles to snakes in jars. On a hot afternoon in August, I walked out of the San Diego Natural History Museum carrying a whale rib, a leopard pelt, a taxidermized weasel and a small piece of fossilized dinosaur…
body: It felt like a heist. These were real specimens that belonged to the museum, not gift shop replicas. But for two weeks, they were mine to take home, display in my living room, even bring to events with my friends.

San Diego, California, has the only natural history museum in the US with a collection of nature specimens that they allow members of the general public to check out and take home, just like checking out books from a library.

Inside the museum, metal shelves of taxidermy fill the space floor to ceiling. Light glints off rows of plexiglass boxes: alert bobcats, their ears perked; birds posed on branches; a jackrabbit suspended in air as if in mid-leap. There are Riker cabinets filled with beetles and butterflies, shelves of pickled sea creatures and snakes in jars, and plastic bins of exotic animal pelts.
Haylie Priest, the loan program’s manager, guided me through the room’s wonders: 1,400 specimens in total, from a megalodon tooth fossil to a king cobra head in a jar.

articles.title: Hair Growth vs Anti-Shed Serums—and Why You Need Both
articles.summary: Experts weigh in on the difference between both serums—and how, when combined, the duo can improve hair density, reduce shed, and boost growth
body: Whether you’re trying to regrow hair after a heavy shed or simply hoping to achieve longer lengths, navigating a hair growth journey comes with plenty of information to digest. There’s also no shortage of products to choose from—particularly the burgeoning scalp serums category. But does what you reach for depend on whether your goal is to encourage growth or slow shedding as much as possible? In short, yes, but the answer is nuanced.

“The primary goal of a hair growth serum is to stimulate new hair growth and increase overall density, whereas an anti-shed serum is designed to reduce shedding and help you retain the hair you already have for longer,” board-certified dermatologist Sejal Shah, MD, tells Vogue. “While the two can overlap, reducing shedding may help improve the appearance of fullness, and some hair growth products may also help minimize shedding, they are not necessarily interchangeable.”

articles.title: The 2026 Telluride Film Festival Is Our Fall Fashion Inspiration
articles.summary: Take a look at the best fashions from the 2026 Telluride Film Festival, from Emma Stone’s buttoned-up look to Rami Malek’s stylish suede jacket.
body: While the Venice Film Festival may be known for its over-the-top glitz and glamour, over in Telluride, Colorado, things are a little bit more, shall we say, down-to-earth.

Running concurrently with Venice, the 2026 Telluride Film Festival offers a vastly different sartorial approach to film promotion, with the stars swapping their custom gowns and heels for jeans and boots. Indeed, fall is well underway in the Rocky Mountains, and this year’s crop of attendees reminds us that there’s much to look forward to when the weather cools down everywhere else.

Layering was top of mind for the celebrity set. Dressed in a jacket, cardigan, and button-up, Emma Stone made the argument that there’s no such thing as too many buttons. Jordan Firstman livened up a white sweater and leather jacket with a whisper of color, the collar of a pale pink crewneck peeking out from his knit. Cara Delevingne and Sofia Coppola, meanwhile, both layered T-shirts with button-ups; the model added a Westernwear touch with her open long-sleeve, while the director kept things classic in a striped shirt over a white tee.
points: Take a look at the best fashions from the 2026 Telluride Film Festival, from Emma Stone’s buttoned-up look to Rami Malek’s stylish suede jacket.

body: Red carpet lovers, it’s your lucky day: The 2026 Venice Film Festival has officially arrived.

The film roster for this year’s festival has plenty of buzzy projects to take in: Among them is Martin McDonagh’s Oscar-tipped black comedy Wild Horse Nine; Lance Oppenheim’s Primetime; a Robert Pattinson-led portrait of To Catch a Predator host Chris Hansen; and Bunker, Florian Zeller’s marital drama starring Penélope Cruz and Javier Bardem.

Better year, however, is what all of these A-listers will be wearing on the step and repeat for the splashy premieres. This is, after all, the festival that last year offered the first glimpses of new-era Chanel, Dior, Versace and Bottega Veneta before their respective runway debuts, and which has given us Lady Gaga’s feathered Valentino couture gown in 2018 and Zendaya’s wet-look Balmain dress in 2021, among other standout moments.

articles.title: In London, artisans are keeping hands-on heritage alive – meet the makers championing the craft revival
articles.summary: Craft is booming – here are the makers taking London's artisanal heritage to new heights
body: When London Craft Week, an annual celebration of the handmade, unfurled across the center of the city this past May, the work of a thousand or so makers bloomed out of every corner. Glassblowers opened up their Deptford workshops. Batik textiles filled the walls of St. James's galleries. Ancient ceramics populated storied auction houses. What's more, long lines amassed to see the works, an undeniable testament to the growing interest in traditional crafts movements and the makers behind them. Case in point: When London Craft Week was launched by founder Guy Salter in 2015, it recorded around 20,000 visitors; this year approximately 250,000 came.
